text: places the picture of sitting room   Scene 5 - Mrs Vane’s sitting room
speaker: C5

text: The Vane’s dingy sitting-room contained one arm-chair. Mrs Vane…
speaker: C5

text: a faded, tired-looking woman,
speaker: Mrs Vane

text: was sitting in it, with her back turned to the shrill intrusive light
speaker: C8

text: Mother, I am so happy and you must be happy, too!
speaker: Sibyl

text: Happy! I am only happy, when I see you act. You must not think of anything but your acting. Mr. Jacobs has been very good to us, and we owe him money.
speaker: Mrs Vane

text: Money? What does money matter? Love is more than money.
speaker: Sibyl

text: Mr. Jacobs has advanced us fifty pounds to pay off our debts and to get a proper outfit for James. He has been most considerate.
speaker: Mrs Vane

text: He is not a gentleman, Mother, and I hate the way he talks to me.
speaker: Sibyl

text: I don't know how we could manage without him.
speaker: Mrs Vane

text: We don't want him any more. Prince Charming is all that matters now. I love him.
speaker: Sibyl

text: Foolish child!
speaker: Mrs Vane

text: I love him because he is what love should be. I am not worthy of him.
speaker: Sibyl

text: My child, you are far too young to think of falling in love. What do you know of this young man? You don't even know his name. The whole thing is most inconvenient, and really, when James is going away to Australia, and I have so much to think of, I must say that you should have shown more consideration. Although, if he is rich ...
speaker: Mrs Vane

text: Ah! Mother let me be happy!
speaker: Sibyl

text: You might keep some of your kisses for me, Sibyl, I think.
speaker: James

text: Ah! but you don't like being kissed, Jim. You are a dreadful old bear.
speaker: Sibyl

text: I want you to come out with me for a walk. I don't suppose I shall ever see this horrid London again. I am sure I don't want to.
speaker: James

text: My son, don't say such dreadful things.
speaker: Mrs Vane

text: Why not, Mother? I mean it.
speaker: James

text: You pain me, my son. When you have made your fortune, in Australia you must come back and assert yourself in London.
speaker: Mrs Vane

text: I should like to make some money to take you and Sibyl off the stage. I hate it.
speaker: James

text: Oh, Jim! How unkind of you! But are you really going for a walk with me? Where shall we go? Let us go to the park.
speaker: Sibyl

text: I am too shabby. Only swell people go to the park.
speaker: James

text: Nonsense, Jim.
speaker: Sibyl

text: Very well, but don't be too long dressing.
speaker: James

text: Mother, you must watch over Sibyl. Don't let her come to any harm.
speaker: James

text: You really talk very strangely. Of course I watch over her.
speaker: Mrs Vane

text: I hear a gentleman comes every night to the theatre and goes behind to talk to her. Is that right?
speaker: James

text: You are speaking about things you don't understand. I myself used to receive many bouquets at one time. That was when acting was really understood. The young man in question is a perfect gentleman. He is always most polite to me. Besides, he has the appearance of being rich, and the flowers he sends are lovely.
speaker: Mrs Vane

text: You don't know his name, though.
speaker: James

text: No, he has not yet revealed his real name. I think it is quite romantic of him. He is probably a member of the aristocracy. To Sibyl he is Prince Charming. I must say. It might be a most brilliant marriage for her
speaker: Mrs Vane

text: Mother there is something I have always wondered. I want you to tell me the truth - Were you married to my father?
speaker: James

text: No.
speaker: Mrs Vane

text: My father was a scoundrel then.
speaker: James

text: I knew he was not free. We loved each other very much. If he had lived, he would have made provision for us. He was a gentleman. Indeed, he was highly connected.
speaker: Mrs Vane

text: I don't care for myself but don't let Sibyl.... It is a gentleman, isn't it, who is in love with her, or says he is? Highly connected, too, I suppose.
speaker: James

text: And rich.
speaker: Mrs Vane

text: Believe me that if this man wrongs my sister, I will find out who he is, track him down, and kill him like a dog. I swear it.
speaker: James

text: How serious you both are. What is the matter?
speaker: Sibyl

text: Nothing. I suppose one must be serious sometimes.
speaker: James

text: They went out into the flickering, wind-blown sunlight and strolled down the dreary Euston Road.
speaker: C2

text: The passersby glanced in wonder at the sullen heavy youth in the company of such a graceful, refined-looking girl.
speaker: C2

text: As they walked Sibyl talked of the future. James bit his underlip with a twitch of pain and his brows knit together into a wedge-like furrow.
speaker: C4

text: You are not listening to a word I am saying. Do say something.
speaker: Sibyl

text: What do you want me to say?
speaker: James

text: Oh! that you will not forget us
speaker: Sibyl

text: You are more likely to forget me than I am to forget you.
speaker: James

text: What do you mean?
speaker: Sibyl

text: You have a new friend, I hear. Who is he? Why have you not told me about him? He means you no good.
speaker: James

text: You must not say anything against him. I love him.
speaker: Sibyl

text: Why, you don't even know his name. Who is he?
speaker: James

text: He is called Prince Charming. Oh, Jim! If you only saw him, you would think him the most wonderful person in the world. I am poor beside him. Poor? What does that matter? When poverty creeps in at the door, love flies in through the window.
speaker: Sibyl

text: He is a gentleman. He wants to enslave you. I want you to beware of him.
speaker: James

text: You dear old Jim, you talk as if you were a hundred. Some day you will be in love yourself. Then you will know what it is.
speaker: Sibyl

text: As sure as there is a God in heaven, if he ever does you any wrong, I shall kill him.
speaker: James

text: You are foolish, Jim. You don't know what you are talking about. Love makes people good, and what you said was wicked.
speaker: Sibyl

text: Sibyl - take care. Mother is no help to you. She doesn't understand how to look after you.
speaker: James

text: Don't be so serious, Jim. I know you would never harm anyone I love, would you?
speaker: Sibyl

text: Not as long as you love him, I suppose.
speaker: James

text: I shall love him forever!
speaker: Sibyl

text: And he?
speaker: James

text: Forever, too!
speaker: Sibyl

text: He had better.
speaker: James
